binaries.name: fsapfsinfo
binaries.why: Inspect an APFS container and its volumes. This experimental libfsapfs build does not support snapshots, Fusion drives or T2 encryption: those are limits of the build, not findings about the evidence, and what it lists is what the installed build parsed (say which). No macOS install route is declared.

binaries.name: log
binaries.why: Apple's own reader for the unified log, present only on macOS: a macOS-host alternative to the pinned unifiedlog_iterator, never a Linux dependency. Record the OS build when it is used.

install.apt: not available on Linux; use the pinned unifiedlog_iterator

binaries.not_in_image: Apple's own reader exists only on macOS. The image uses Mandiant's pinned unifiedlog_iterator on Linux.

binaries.name: mac_apt.py
binaries.why: A plugin-based artefact parser for macOS and iOS evidence, pinned at 1.33.2 and installed in the amd64 worker image only: its statx helper stops at import on Linux arm64. The project describes its input as E01, DMG and sparse images and UAC and Velociraptor collections; none of that is tested in this repository. Its Python dependencies are installed from its requirements file without a hash lock. Whether a plugin supports the subject's macOS build is for the examiner to establish; no wrapper or skill of this pack drives it beyond naming it in triage/system-profile.

install.apt: pinned source 1.33.2 (install.source), amd64 only: its statx helper knows no aarch64 syscall number, so it stops at import on Linux arm64

binaries.name: unifiedlog_iterator
binaries.why: Read modern macOS and iOS unified log archives off a Mac and keep every decoded entry as JSONL. unified_log records the reader's version in each answer; whether this version decodes the logs of a given macOS build is not established here, so check the version the evidence carries.
